sentence: This project builds a compact MRI scanner that maps the brain shifts that occur during surgery onto preoperative images.
This project studies how genetic and environmental factors shape the behavior of human cells.
This project collects, processes and distributes human fetal tissues to biomedical scientists for their research.
This project tests how biomaterials that grow blood vessels and add heart muscle cells change heart function after a heart attack.
This project tries to find genes and variants that cause congenital diaphragmatic hernia, a birth defect, and checks them in mouse models.
This project studies the molecular mechanisms that control neurotransmitter release during synaptic transmission in the brain.
This project tries to find out whether mitochondrial fusion helps colorectal cancer cells survive when therapies block a pathway.
This project combines a handheld thermal ablation device with a digital colposcope so one instrument can triage and treat cervical precancer.
This project tries to find out which microbial and host factors make gingival inflammatory responses vary across people.
This project studies how HIV and smoking disrupt the airway microRNAome and the signaling pathways that lead to disease.
This project studies how members of a family of solute carrier proteins work in immune cells during the immune response to tumors.
This project uses genome sequencing, blood testing and fruit flies to learn more about diseases in people who lack cellular organelles called peroxisomes.
This project tests how losing a glutamate transporter in astrocytes affects blood vessels, metabolism and neural network activity in mouse models of Alzheimer's disease.
This project supports a clinical research site that helps test therapies for people with neurological disorders.
This project uses mouse models and human biomarker measures to find out what reactive astrocytes do in Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.
This project studies how amyloid forms differently in inhibitory and excitatory neurons and how that affects learning and memory in Alzheimer's disease.
This project tests whether electronic health record data and ultra-widefield color fundus photography can help predict retinal tears and detachments.
This project builds an imaging toolkit to show how an antibody kills cancer cells in animal models of triple negative breast cancer.
